exact_intake_statement: Is there a universal positive lower bound for the Euclidean Cheeger constant of every isotropic log-concave probability measure, in every dimension?
intake_evidence: SOURCE_RECOVERY.json: brain_bundle_C006p01.json entry op-p0017; ranking CSV line 548
exact_primary_cheeger_form: For every dimension and every full-dimensional log-concave probability mu with finite covariance Sigma, h(mu)>=c/sqrt(||Sigma||_op), for a single universal c>0. With E X=0 and Sigma=I this becomes h(mu)>=c.
exact_primary_poincare_form: There exists one universal C<infinity such that every integer d>=1, every isotropic log-concave probability mu on R^d, and every locally Lipschitz f in L^2(mu) with finite gradient energy satisfy Var_mu(f)<=C integral |grad f|^2 dmu. In full-dimensional nonisotropic coordinates, C_P(mu)<=C ||Cov(mu)||_op.
